verdict: Google Ads drove all $1,110.70 in spend over 28 days with 12 conversions, but a 50.52% week-over-week spend drop and zero tracked leads flagged in the system signal a likely conversion tracking gap rather than a true lead drought. GBP engagement also fell sharply by 71.11% week-over-week, suggesting overall demand softening that warrants an immediate audit of lead form and call tracking setup.

performance.verdict: Leads are a measurement ghost — GHL has 46 opps, Google has 12 conversions, system shows zero.

findings.text: 28-day leads tracked = 0, but GHL shows 46 opportunities created and Google Ads logged 12 conversions — attribution is broken, not demand.
Booking bot battle-test was due 2026-07-31 — no completion event recorded; speed-to-lead automations remain unvalidated with intake seat potentially empty since 7/7.

Spend is wildly erratic: 7 zero-spend days in 45, ranging $0–$130.18/day; 3-day signal (Aug 25–27: $15.83, $10.57, $19.61) vs prior 3 (Aug 22–24: $0, $62.48, $16.46) shows low but inconsistent pacing well below the ~$46/day 28-day average.
GBP actions collapsed to 0 for Aug 25–27 (last 3 days), vs 8 on Aug 24 and a 28-day total of 109 — consistent with Windsor data lag flagged in SOW, but worth watching.
Search clicks rose 41.67% week-over-week (7d delta), with Aug 23–26 showing 1, 5, 5, 4 clicks — organic intent is intact while paid lead capture is broken.

suggestions.text: Audit GHL lead source mapping and Google Ads conversion tag — 12 conversions recorded but 0 attributed; fix before any budget move.
suggestions.monday_update: Google Ads logged 12 conversions and GHL shows 46 opportunities created over 28 days, yet the performance system reads zero tracked leads — attribution is broken somewhere between the conversion tag and GHL source mapping. Pull the Google Ads conversion action, check the tag fires on thank-you/call events, and reconcile GHL contact sources against the 46 opp records. Success = leads_7d_pct returns a real number and GHL source breakdown shows a Google or paid channel row. Target: resolved by 2026-09-01.

suggestions.text: Confirm who owns intake in GHL since Vivian left 7/7 — speed-to-lead automations may be routing to an empty seat.
suggestions.monday_update: Vivian (dispatch) left 7/7 and the booking bot battle-test due 7/31 has no completion event. Speed-to-lead automations are pointing at a seat that may be unmanned, meaning inbound leads from the 46 GHL opportunities could be going unworked. Confirm the active GHL login owner with Xavier or Nader, verify after-hours coverage is routed correctly, and run the booking bot battle-test end-to-end. Success = named owner confirmed in writing and bot test passed. Target: 2026-09-01.

suggestions.text: Watch GBP actions — 3 consecutive zero days (Aug 25–27) may be Windsor lag; re-check natively on 2026-08-31.
suggestions.monday_update: GBP actions hit zero for Aug 25, 26, and 27 after registering 8 on Aug 24 and 109 over 28 days total. The SOW flags Windsor data lag on the last 2–3 days of any GBP window, so this may not be a real drop. Pull the native GBP Insights dashboard on 2026-08-31 to confirm. Success = native GBP shows actions consistent with the prior week average (~4–5/day); if native also reads zero for 3+ days, escalate as a separate finding.
